sections.heading: What this dossier is
sections.body: Invest 97L is live in the north-central Gulf. Storm Atlas neither forecasts it nor states a landfall. The archive holds twelve storms formed within 250 km of the declared pre-genesis reference cell 28.0°N 88.7°W, August–September, from 1971. Conditional on formation, silent on whether it forms.

sections.heading: Why 28.0°N 88.7°W and not the live centre
sections.body:
The query runs at a declared pre-genesis reference cell, 28.0°N 88.7°W, not the live centre, 27.4°N 90.7°W. 97L has not formed: no genesis, no b-deck. The live centre moves; a published question does not.

Cell, radius and month window are analyst choices, declared before the query, not re-fitted after or derived from the live centre. The same cell at 150 km returns N=5 and refuses every rate: this frame clears the minimum sample, a tighter one does not. A constraint on publication, not validation.

The question: if a cyclone formed within 250 km of this cell, what happened next? Silent on whether 97L forms, or forms inside the cell.

sections.heading: Reading the outcome panel
sections.body:
Scoreable rows are exact n/N with the engine's 95% Wilson interval. Read the interval, not the point estimate: at N=12 the bands are wide by construction and the archive will not narrow them.

The CONUS rows are two questions. Any intensity is 10 of 12 (83.3%, 95% Wilson 55-95%); hurricane force, 1 of 12 (8.3%, 95% Wilson 1-35%).

Two rows are stamped unscoreable; an interval still prints beside them, void. Both Hawaii rows print 0/12 and 0.0% [0-24%]: an artefact of the count, not a low probability. No Gulf cohort could score Hawaii, so that refusal costs nothing. The refusals that bite: no state-level row exists at any sample size, and at 150 km this cell refuses every rate.

sections.heading: Radius, month window and season floor
sections.body:
Every citation declares three filters: radius, month window, 1971 season floor. Two are varied here.

At 250 km, August–September, from 1971: N=12, SUFFICIENT, rates publish. At 150 km: N=5, below the minimum sample of 10, every rate REFUSED; counts print, rates do not. All months, 250 km: N=17, SUFFICIENT, rows move: CONUS any 13 of 17 (76.5%, 95% Wilson 53-90%), CONUS ≥64 kt 2 of 17 (11.8%, 95% Wilson 3-34%).

Three frames on the hurricane-force trigger row: 1 of 12, 0 of 5 (refused), 2 of 17. The frame decides whether the instrument answers, and moves the answer. Radius and month window sit in the published question, not a footnote; buyers should ask what an unshown frame returns.

The 1971 floor is not varied: no floor-off variant exists here, so its effect on N=12 is not shown. Declared, not tested.

sections.heading: Historical transit times
sections.body:
Timing quantiles sit outside the minimum-sample rule, unstamped at any n. Medians from genesis: TS 21 h (n=10, p25 7.5, p75 33); Cat 1 36 h (n=3, p25 33, p75 84); Cat 3 72 h (n=2, p25 69, p75 75); CONUS crossing 65.5 h (n=22, p25 36.75, p75 176.25).

Only TS clears the 10-case threshold. Cat 1 is the three storms behind the 3/12 rate, Cat 3 two: a spread, not a distribution.

n=22 counts landfall rows, not storms: 10 of 12 crossed, FERN 1971 supplying 12 of the 22, five Louisiana, seven Texas. Over half that spread, the 176.25 h quartile included, is one track re-counted, not twelve independent cases.

Intervals from each member's own genesis; no lead time for 97L, which has none.

sections.heading: The analog plate
sections.body:
Eight of twelve print under the archive's rule: majors (≥96 kt), hurricanes (≥64 kt), peak wind descending, ties by season. The four unshown peak no higher than 50 kt. Selection, not ranking: it over-represents the intense end.

ANITA 1977: 150 kt peak, ashore Tamaulipas, Mexico at 120 kt. ALICIA 1983: 100 kt peak, ashore Texas at 100 kt. Storm facts, not rates, never counted into one.

No similarity metric; every member weighted 1.0, none a closer or likelier match. Tracks are history, not a cone.

sections.heading: COMMERCIAL READ — interpretation, not a rate
sections.body:
• Insured-region adjacency. These rows are CONUS-wide, not Gulf-coast: the archive scores no sub-CONUS region, and crossings include Florida as well as Texas and Louisiana. Against a Gulf-facing book: a national-coastline prior, not a Gulf number. 10 of 12 crossed at any intensity (83.3%, 95% Wilson 55-95%); 1 of 12 at ≥64 kt (8.3%, 95% Wilson 1-35%), the second a subset of the first. A hurricane-force attachment rests on one archived event, 1-35% band. Bound or challenge a rate set elsewhere; do not derive one.
  • Energy adjacency. The cell sits in north-central Gulf production and marine-logistics geography. Transit to a CONUS crossing is a median 65.5 h; its upper quartile is largely one 1971 track re-counted, not twelve independent cases. For shut-in and re-staging: a historical statistic, not a schedule.
  • Parametric triggers. Class attainment: Cat 1 3 of 12 (25.0%, 95% Wilson 9-53%), Cat 3 2 of 12 (16.7%, 95% Wilson 5-45%). N=12 returns intervals too wide to price a trigger; they bound one and show a counterparty what the record does and does not contain.
  • BASIS RISK — same genesis cell does not mean same landfall. ANITA 1977 formed 126 km from this cell and struck Tamaulipas; ALICIA 1983 formed 194 km from it and struck Texas. One cell, two coasts.
  • BASIS RISK — intensity class is not local outcome. Peak is not landfall intensity. FERN 1971 peaked at 80 kt; Louisiana crossings recorded at 25 kt, Texas crossings between 43 and 60 kt. No landfall row for that storm reaches its peak.
  • BASIS RISK — a CONUS row is not a state row. The archive records state names in landfall rows and publishes no state-level rate. CONUS and CONUS ≥64 kt are the rows that exist; any TX/LA/MS-AL-FL or Gulf-state rate would be manufactured, and none appears here.

sections.heading: What is not here
sections.body:
Refused by the instrument. No Hawaii rate: hawaii:any OUT OF SCOPE for a North Atlantic cohort; hawaii:hurricane BASE RATE ONLY, 2 events archive-wide against a 10-event minimum. No rates at all at 150 km, where N=5 and every row returned REFUSED.

Out of scope by contract. No state-level landfall row, and nothing here is a sub-CONUS rate. No P(forms): the engine is genesis-conditioned and takes formation as given, so the 70%/70% (48h/7d) on AL97 is NHC's, printed as theirs. The two do not chain: NHC's covers genesis anywhere in the Northern Gulf of America area it named; the archive's rows, only genesis within 250 km of 28.0°N 88.7°W. Different conditioning sets, different producers, different scoring. Multiplying them assumes 97L forms inside the cell: the reader's assumption, not this dossier's. No unconditional number is computed here, no forecast track, no cone, no landfall call for 97L.

sections.body: Storm Atlas is a research-only historical engine. It answers one fixed question: from this declared genesis condition, in this season window, what did the record go on to do? N = 12, ESS 12, SUFFICIENT against a minimum sample of 10.

sections.heading: Why a replayable cohort is trigger documentation
sections.body:
A parametric trigger’s basis-risk file needs a prior a counterparty can reopen, not a number in a deck. The cohort is a URL: cell, radius, month window, season floor and methodology version travel in it, so the same query returns the same n/N, the same interval and the same stamps on any desk.

The denominator is named. Twelve storms, each listed, each with its own recorded landfalls — a reviewer can check the count rather than accept it.

sections.heading: Near-misses: where the basis risk is
sections.body:
A near-miss is a cohort member that satisfies the genesis rule and then fails the condition a trigger would be written on.

  • Anita 1977. Formed 126 km from the cell; ashore in Tamaulipas, Mexico at 120 kt. Inside the cohort, outside the CONUS row.
  • Alicia 1983. Formed 194 km out, ashore in Texas at 100 kt — the single member behind CONUS — ≥64 kt at 1 of 12 (8.3%, 95% Wilson 1-35%). That is a CONUS row, not a Texas one: the archive does not score state-level landfall. At 150 km Alicia is not a member at all, and every rate refuses.
  • Barry 2019. Formed 110 km from the cell with a 65 kt Louisiana landfall, but its 11 July genesis falls outside August–September: not in this cohort. It is the closest thing in the record to the event a trigger here would be written for. Read the misses first.

sections.heading: Basis risk — read before writing the trigger
sections.body:
• Same genesis cell ≠ same landfall. Twelve storms formed inside one 250 km circle and went to Texas, Louisiana, Florida and Tamaulipas.
  • Same class ≠ same local outcome. The archive scores a crossing and its intensity, not a footprint, a surge or a loss.
  • A CONUS row is not a state row. No state-level landfall is scored, at any radius or sample size. None is supplied here.
  • The interval is the precision. 1 of 12 is 8.3% with a 95% Wilson band of 1-35%. The band is the finding; the point estimate is not.
  • A refused row is not a zero. At 150 km the same question returns RATE REFUSED, and a stamped row’s 0.0% is voided by its stamp.

sections.heading: Where this sits in the workflow
sections.body: Cohort research, trigger-threshold design and counterparty explanation. Not live pricing of a running event: Storm Atlas holds no live view, and every rate here is conditional on a formation it does not forecast.

sections.heading: Geography is not a probability
sections.body: Landfall resolves to region, not state. The archive scores CONUS, Mexico, Caribbean, Central America, Hawaii and unattributed, each in an "any" and a ">=64 kt" form. On this cohort both Hawaii rows are refused: HAWAII — any is OUT OF SCOPE -- unscoreable here, HAWAII — >=64 kt is BASE RATE ONLY -- unscoreable. There is no Texas row, no Louisiana row and no Gulf-state row to quote: the archive does not score states at all, so CONUS and CONUS >=64 kt are the rows that bear on a Gulf question. The paths on the plate are drawn tracks of the 8 printed cohort members — geometry, not a rate, and not an analog for 97L.

sections.heading: Commercial reading — what the rows cover
sections.body:
Two hurricane landfalls, opposite sides of the basin. The cohort's scored hurricane rows are CONUS — >=64 kt at 1 of 12 (8.3%, 95% Wilson 1-35%) and MEXICO — >=64 kt at 1 of 12 (8.3%, 95% Wilson 1-35%). ANITA 1977 is the Mexican one, ashore in Tamaulipas at 120 kt; ALICIA 1983 is the CONUS one, ashore in Texas at 100 kt. Those are facts about two storms; the rates above them are region rows — a CONUS row, not a Texas one — and the archive does not score state-level landfall. Neither region row is a terminal, a platform or a refinery: region-to-asset is basis risk the archive does not carry.

Severity resolves only to the intensity ladder the archive publishes: reached TS 10 of 12 (83.3%, 95% Wilson 55-95%), Cat 1 3 of 12 (25.0%, 9-53%), Cat 3 2 of 12 (16.7%, 5-45%), Cat 5 1 of 12 (8.3%, 1-35%).

sections.heading: Read the band, not the point
sections.body: Every scored row is a band. CONUS — >=64 kt on this cohort is 1 of 12 (8.3%, 95% Wilson 1-35%), and the interval, not the 8.3%, is the research input. Twelve members makes it wide by construction: one member moves the answer by a twelfth. Tightening the aperture does not buy precision — it removes the answer. The same cell at 150 km returns N=5 against min sample 10; that cohort is stamped BELOW MIN SAMPLE and every row comes back RATE REFUSED.

sections.heading: What this is not
sections.body: No prices, no trades, no view on gas, power, refined products or freight. No state rates — the archive does not score states, and no named member's landfall is converted into one. Rows are genesis-conditioned and assume formation: not P(forms), not a cone, not a track for 97L. The NHC advisory is the forecast; this is the record standing behind it.

answers.commercial: Worked here: the 97L cohort returns CONUS ≥64 kt at 1 of 12 — 8.3%, 95% Wilson 1-35% — on a denominator a counterparty can open and read storm by storm. The interval, not the point, is what a candidate trigger must survive. No price call, no recommendation, no skill claim.

sections.body: A research-only historical genesis/outcome engine for the North Atlantic and East Pacific: give it an observed genesis point or a declared pre-genesis reference cell and it returns what the record did next as exact n/N with a 95% Wilson interval, names every storm in the denominator, and refuses what the record cannot carry.

• Condition on a point. An observed genesis position or a declared pre-genesis reference cell, with a stated radius and month window. The 1971 season floor is declared, not preferred: East Pacific majors were under-observed before it, and a cohort reaching behind it is warned rather than pooled silently. Rates assume formation — not P(forms), not a live feed, not a cone.
  • Retrieve the analog tracks. Every storm in the cohort; representative members under a stated rule, with genesis date, distance from the cell, peak and their own recorded landfalls. No similarity metric exists, so nothing is ranked a closest or best analog.
  • Compare contract-row frequencies. Reached TD, TS and Cat 1 through Cat 5, each exact n/N with its 95% Wilson interval. Time-to-threshold medians carry their own n: the min-sample gate governs rates, not medians.
  • Inspect the landfall rows. conus, mexico, caribbean, central_america, hawaii, unattributed — each an “any” and a ≥64 kt pair. Which of the twelve score is a property of the cohort. State-level landfall is not scored; a sub-region is a fact about a named storm, never a rate.
  • Read the refusals as output. Below min sample: counts, no rate, no interval. Out of scope, or too rare archive-wide: a status beside a figure it voids. Hawaii ≥64 kt is base rate only, 2 events archive-wide against 10.
  • Carry it into the work. Set a threshold and count the members that cross it; they are named, so the count is checkable. Move the cell and watch N and the refusal move with it. Hand a reviewer the URL, not a number.

An interpolated fix never establishes a threshold crossing, so time-to-hurricane is never dated off a wind nobody measured. A segment crossing publishes no Saffir-Simpson class where the bracketing fixes disagree — the interpolated wind stays on the row, labelled by detection method; the class does not. A cohort’s defining variable is not reported back as an outcome of it, with one exception left in the open: every cohort returns reached TD at 100%, because a cohort is storms that formed. Below min sample a rate is refused rather than estimated: the same 97L cell at 150 km returns 5 storms against a minimum of 10, and every rate reads RATE REFUSED. An absent outcome is not a zero — an unrecorded intensity leaves the denominator and is counted on its own. Every figure, refusals included, carries METHODOLOGY 1.1.0, PACK 134661125525f27a and a URL that reproduces it.

A browser and replayable cohort URLs. A URL carries the cell, radius, season floor, month window, basin and methodology version, so a reviewer opens the same cohort and reads the same counts, rates, intervals and refusals. The pack stamp is a hash of every table it was built from: a figure whose stamp does not match is not the same figure.
PROPOSED / PILOT — not available today. Exportable charts. An API. Recurring institutional briefs. None of the three exists yet.

Three cohorts, as the engine returned them. The cell is an input, not an observation: 97L is read at a desk-declared reference cell, 28.0°N 88.7°W — not the disturbance’s position — and the URL records the choice, so a reviewer can move it and watch the answer move. Karina is read at its observed genesis: reached Cat 4 is 1 of 14 [1-31%], reached Cat 5 is 0 of 14 [0-22%], and Karina is already Cat 4. That is the record’s frequency at the moment of formation, not revised because this storm intensified.
